issue.description:
New src/bead_store/bead_cli.rs implementing the existing BeadStore trait against bead-rs (`bead`). Surface enumerated from ~/bead-rs/src/cli.rs at commit fa30574.

Dialect specifics (each differs from bf in a way that fails loudly at runtime and silently in review):
- claim/release/clear_assignee: plain `update --status ... --assignee ...` / `update --status open --clear-assignee`. bead-rs UpdateOptions (cli.rs:444) KEPT the --assignee that bf 0.4.1 removed, so these are SIMPLER here than on bf — no batch emulation needed.
- claim_auto: `claim --assignee A --json`. Omit --model/--harness/--harness-version — bead-rs ClaimOptions (cli.rs:370) does not accept them. Selection falls back to bead-rs own --policy (default fifo-v1).
- create_bead: `--description` (not --body), repeated `--label`, no --json. bead-rs create prints the bare issue ID on stdout.
- add_dependency: `--kind blocks` (not --type). Confirm positional order against the installed binary before landing.
- full_rebuild: bead-rs `sync --import-only` REQUIRES --input plus exactly one of --restore-into-empty / --merge (SyncCommand, cli.rs:667). The current bare call would fail.
- list/show/update --status/reopen/close --reason/label add|remove/doctor [--repair]/sync --flush-only all match and need no special handling.
- split_bead: deliberately NOT overridden. bead-rs has no `batch` subcommand, so it inherits the non-atomic trait default (:646-668) and its documented orphaned-child crash window. Log at split time that the atomic path is unavailable on this backend.

Acceptance criteria:
- Every trait method implemented; no todo!()/unimplemented!().
- Known limitations (no atomic split, no velocity-scoring metadata) are logged at runtime, not silently swallowed.
- fmt + clippy + full suite green on iad-ci.

single run, then compiles 244 crates cold.

Worse, that image was last pushed 2026-04-25 -- over three months ago -- and
nothing in iad-ci rebuilds it, so its baked dependency layer no longer matches
Cargo.toml (opentelemetry 0.31, tonic 0.14 postdate it) and its rustup predates
the pinned-toolchain fix in rust-toolchain.toml.

Do:
- add a needle-ci-builder WorkflowTemplate + sensor in declarative-config under
  k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/, triggered by changes to Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock or
  ci/Dockerfile.ci*
- pin a semver tag, never latest and never a bare git SHA
- switch needle-ci's container image to it and delete the inline apt/rustup/gh
  install block

Blocked by the Cargo.lock bead: Dockerfile.ci-deps does COPY Cargo.toml Cargo.lock.

Acceptance: a needle-ci run performs no apt-get and no rustup install, and skips
compiling unchanged dependencies.

BrCliBeadStore::add_dependency (src/bead_store/mod.rs:1579) and BfCliBeadStore::add_dependency (:2288) both emit `dep add <blocked> <blocker> --type blocks`. bf 0.4.1 signature is `bf dep add [OPTIONS] <BLOCKER>` — exactly ONE positional (the blocker), with the blocked bead passed as `--blocks <BLOCKS>`. `-t, --type` does exist and defaults to blocks.

So the second positional is an unexpected argument. Note prompt/mod.rs:325 already tells the agent the CORRECT form (`bf dep add <blocker-id> --blocks <blocked-id>`) — it is the store code that is stale, not the prompt.

Deliverables:
- Both impls emit `dep add <blocker> --blocks <blocked>`; drop the redundant explicit --type blocks (it is the default) or keep it as `-t blocks`, but verify against the installed bf first.
- Confirm argument ORDER semantics empirically before landing — get it backwards and dependency edges invert, which is worse than failing loudly.
- Same treatment for remove_dependency (:1667) — verify `bf dep remove` signature.
- Fixture-CLI argv assertion tests for add and remove.

Acceptance criteria:
- A real round-trip against a scratch .beads workspace proves the edge lands in the intended direction (blocker blocks blocked), not merely that the command exits 0.
- fmt + clippy + full suite green on iad-ci.

See docs/adr/013-pluggable-bead-cli-backends.md, Addendum.

zero commits. Investigation (2026-08-17) found the underlying claude

(internal/server/route_table.go + route_table_test.go) -- it just never
got committed or closed, matching needle-55ec0193's leak exactly. Left a
comment there with the full repro.

But there's a second, distinct problem this incident exposed: the
`needle-stable` binary these long-lived workers are running
(/home/coding/.needle/bin/needle-stable, confirmed via readlink that
/home/coding/.local/bin/needle is a symlink to the same file) was built
2026-08-15 22:38. Two fixes for exactly this failure class have landed in
NEEDLE's own source since then and are already merged to main:

  - ecc207d fix(needle-f6afd68c): reclaim stale live claims (2026-08-17 01:03)
  - 33b16ad fix(needle-3653fee9): repair dispatch claim verification and
    unblock CI (2026-08-17 09:55)

`git merge-base --is-ancestor ecc207d <the running binary's build commit>`
confirms the fix is NOT an ancestor of what's deployed. The seam-1, seam-2,
and luna-seam tmux sessions (all `--count 1`, running since 2026-08-15,
still alive right now) are STILL running the pre-fix binary and will keep
being vulnerable to the exact bug class NEEDLE's own team already fixed,
indefinitely, until someone notices and manually kills + relaunches them
on a freshly built binary. There is no version check, no self-restart, no
notification that a running worker's binary is stale relative to a landed
fix.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THIS ONE INCIDENT

Every fix filed against the claim-leak/mend-reclaim failure class (this
one, needle-55ec0193, needle-44e7e5cd, needle-f6afd68c) only helps workers
that get relaunched after the fix ships. Long-lived `--count 1` workers
(the normal dispatch pattern per this fleet's own conventions) are
designed to run indefinitely without ever being relaunched, so in
practice NONE of them will ever pick up a fix unless a human happens to
notice and cycle them. This silently defeats the entire fix-and-ship loop
for this whole bug class -- the fleet keeps reproducing bugs the team
believes it already closed.

FIX (interim, no protocol change): a periodic self-check in the worker's
outer loop (`needle run --count 1`) that compares its own binary's build
version/commit against the latest available `needle-stable` on disk (or a
configured source), and if stale, exits cleanly after its current claim
so the next launch (or a supervisor) picks up the new binary. Must NOT
kill a bead mid-dispatch -- check between cycles, not during one.

FIX (durable): `needle supervise` (already deployed for SEAM as
`needle-supervisor-seam`, itself currently inactive/near-zero CPU since
launch per the same investigation) should own binary-freshness as part of
its job: detect a newer `needle-stable` build, drain+relaunch its
supervised workers onto it, the same way it's meant to auto-scale worker
count to queue depth. Worth checking why the SEAM supervisor process
itself shows ~13s cumulative CPU across ~30h uptime and an activity log
silent since its startup messages -- it may share the same
never-cycles-so-never-updates problem, or may be stuck/dead outright;
that wasn't root-caused in this pass and is worth a separate look.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- A running --count 1 worker detects when the on-disk needle-stable
  binary is newer than the one it was launched with.
- It exits cleanly between dispatch cycles (never mid-claim) so a
  supervisor or relaunch picks up the new binary.
- needle supervise actively relaunches workers onto a fresh binary
  rather than just scaling worker count.
- A test or documented manual check confirms a long-lived worker
  eventually running a fix that landed after it started.
issue.title: Long-running --count 1 workers never pick up a rebuilt binary after a fix lands

PROOF INVALIDATED (2026-08-12) — flagged during the ADR-002 field-guide independent review.

This bead closed on the claim that the rehydration procedure was proven on fixtures with rehearsal and rollback. The rehearsal it validated runs `bead sync flush-only` followed by `bead sync import-only --restore-into-empty`. That round trip is now demonstrated to lose data silently:

  revision            3 -> 1        (bf-4hr30)
  issue_data          1 -> 0        (bf-xq4ds)
  external_references 1 -> 0        (bf-53b91)

Reproduced with bead 0.1.1 against a fully-populated workspace. Labels, dependencies and events survive; the three above do not, and none of the losses raise an error.

The external-reference loss is the one that voids this bead's claim outright: external references are the sole public mechanism binding a rehydrated bead to its source tracker ID, so the rehearsal step destroys exactly the traceability it exists to demonstrate. A rollback based on that checkpoint cannot restore what was never written.

The rehydration playbook bead bf-2yxoi is now blocked on bf-4qyz7 (round-trip fidelity conformance test), bf-4hr30, bf-xq4ds and bf-53b91.

Recommend reopening this bead once those close, and re-running the proof against a round trip that has fidelity coverage. Not reopening it unilaterally — that is the owner's call.

issue.description:
## What

`TelemetryEvent` (src/telemetry/mod.rs:55) — the record written to
`<log_dir>/<worker>-<session>.jsonl` by `FileSink`, and to stdout by
`StdoutSink` — carries timestamp, event_type, worker_id, session_id, sequence,
bead_id, workspace, data, duration_ms, trace_id, span_id.

It carries **no host and no user at all**.

Note the asymmetry with the OTLP path: that one already stamps `host.name` and
(after [[needle-7fa44b83]]) `process.owner`. The JSONL path has neither, so the
two sinks describe the same event with different identifying power.

## Why it matters more than it looks

JSONL is not just a local file. The needle-pod design tails it to stdout for a
Vector agent to collect, and **JSONL lines are shipped and indexed
individually**. A line that does not name its own host and user cannot be
attributed once it is out of the file it came from — the only identity it
carries is `worker_id`/`session_id`, which are opaque without a second lookup.

Vector stamps pod/namespace/cluster for pod-collected logs, but bare-metal
fleet logs on ex44 and lab get no such enrichment, which is precisely where
'which box, which account' is the question being asked.

## Decision (do not re-litigate this in the implementation)

Add the two fields to `TelemetryEvent` itself, next to `worker_id`/`session_id`,
rather than emitting them once in a session-header record.

They are session-constant, so a header would be less redundant — but it would
also be useless: consumers receive lines independently, and a header record is
not guaranteed to reach the same shard, index or retention window as the lines
it describes. The envelope already repeats `session_id` on every line for the
same reason. Two short strings per line is the proportionate cost of each line
being self-contained.

## How

Reuse the `process_owner()` helper from [[needle-7fa44b83]] and
`gethostname()` (already a dependency). Resolve both ONCE at telemetry
construction and copy them onto each event — do not call `getpwuid_r` or
`gethostname` per event; these sinks are on the hot path for every dispatch.

The same numeric-uid fallback applies: the pods run `runAsUser: 1000` and may
have no passwd entry.

## Blocked by

[[needle-7fa44b83]] — that bead introduces `process_owner()`. Working these
concurrently means two workers implement the same helper twice, which is the
duplicate-work failure this repo has hit before.

## Compatibility

`TelemetryEvent` is `Deserialize` as well as `Serialize`, and existing JSONL
files on disk will not have these fields. Add them so that old records still
parse — a `#[serde(default)]` — or the log-reading paths (`LogsFilter`, the
cost summaries) will fail on every pre-existing file. Verify by reading a JSONL
file written before the change.

## Acceptance criteria

- A newly written JSONL line contains both the host and the user.
- The same values appear on stdout-sink output.
- A JSONL file written before this change still parses.
- `gethostname`/`getpwuid_r` are called once per process, not once per event.
issue.title: JSONL telemetry events carry neither host nor user; add both to the envelope

issue.close_reason: Fix already fully implemented in src/commit_hook.rs. Lines 103-115 check is_head_pushed() before amending, using git branch -r --contains HEAD. Both acceptance tests (skips_trailer_injection_when_head_already_pushed and injects_trailer_when_head_not_pushed) exist and pass. No code changes needed.
issue.description:
PROBLEM: src/commit_hook.rs (inject_bead_id_trailer, ~lines 34-138) runs `git commit --amend` on workspace HEAD to add a `Bead-Id: <id>` trailer. It is invoked on the worker success path at src/worker/mod.rs:3004-3015 whenever a successful bead produced commits. But the default agent prompt (src/prompt/mod.rs:52) explicitly instructs agents to `git commit`, then `git push` — so by the time the amend runs, HEAD is usually ALREADY pushed to origin. The amend then rewrites a published commit: the local branch holds amended X-prime while origin holds X, nothing ever pushes X-prime (NEEDLE does not push), and the next `git push` from that shared checkout is rejected non-fast-forward, forcing a duplicate-content merge in an environment where force-push is banned. This recurs after every successful bead with commits. commit_hook.rs contains NO upstream/remote containment check (grep for upstream, origin, or @{u} in the file: zero hits).

FIX: before amending, detect whether HEAD is contained in any remote-tracking ref (e.g. `git branch -r --contains HEAD` non-empty, or `git merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD @{u}` when an upstream exists). If pushed, skip the amend and log at info level. Unpushed HEAD behavior stays unchanged. Secondary observation (do not scope-creep; note-only): the flock at src/commit_hook.rs:58-72 serializes other trailer injectors but NOT a sibling plain `git commit` landing between the subject verify and the amend; re-reading HEAD immediately before amending narrows that window.

ACCEPTANCE (verify inside the repo): (1) new test that creates a temp workspace with a local bare remote, commits with the bead id in the subject, pushes, then calls inject_bead_id_trailer — asserts HEAD SHA unchanged and no trailer added; (2) a companion test with an UNPUSHED commit still gets the trailer amended; (3) `cargo test` for the touched targets passes; `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy` clean on touched files.
issue.notes: Verification complete: the fix is already fully implemented in src/commit_hook.rs. Lines 103-115 check if HEAD is pushed using is_head_pushed() helper (lines 244-271, uses git branch -r --contains HEAD). Both required tests exist and pass: skips_trailer_injection_when_head_already_pushed and injects_trailer_when_head_not_pushed. cargo fmt --check and cargo clippy are clean. No changes needed.
issue.title: commit_hook: skip Bead-Id trailer amend when HEAD is already pushed — amend rewrites published commits after every successful bead

issue.description:
## Problem

`config::Backend` (src/config/mod.rs:436) derives Debug/Clone/PartialEq/Eq but
has no `Display` impl, unlike its sibling `config::BeadBackend`
(src/config/mod.rs:391), which does.

This was one of the five compile errors that made main unbuildable
(fixed in b538d06): src/canary/mod.rs used `%backend_type` in a `tracing::info!`
and `{}` in a `bail!`, both of which require Display.

## Current workaround

b538d06 debug-formats it instead — `?backend_type` in the tracing call and
`{:?}` in the bail. That compiles and is correct, but it is inconsistent:
the same log line now prints `backend=bead-forge` (BeadBackend, Display) next to
`resolved_backend=Bf` (Backend, Debug), and the same split shows up in the
"binary not found" error text.

The workaround was deliberately confined to src/canary/mod.rs rather than fixing
it at the source, because src/config/mod.rs had ~44 lines of another worker's
uncommitted in-flight edits at the time and committing that file would have
swept up unrelated work.

## Deliverables

- Add `impl std::fmt::Display for Backend` in src/config/mod.rs, mirroring the
  BeadBackend impl and using the same user-facing spellings
  (Backend::Bf -> "bead-forge", Backend::Bead -> "bead-rs").
- Revert the canary workaround to `%backend_type` / `{}` and drop the
  explanatory comment above the tracing call.

## Acceptance

- `cargo check --lib` and `cargo clippy --lib` clean.
- The canary "bead backend validated" log line renders both backend fields in
  the same human-readable spelling.
issue.title: config::Backend has no Display impl — canary debug-formats it as a workaround

issue.description:
## Scope

Add an explicit opt-out mechanism to bypass checksum verification in `install.sh`. The flag must be clearly named (e.g., `--skip-checksum` or `NEEDLE_SKIP_CHECKSUM=1`) and output a conspicuous warning when used.

## Acceptance

- `--skip-checksum` flag bypasses checksum verification
- Or equivalently clear environment variable: `NEEDLE_SKIP_CHECKSUM=1`
- Opt-out outputs a warning message that is impossible to miss:
  - Use stderr, not stdout
  - Include words "WARNING", "security risk", "checksum verification disabled"
  - Example: "WARNING: Checksum verification disabled. Installing without verification is a security risk."
- Opt-out is covered by a test
- Documentation in the bead body explains the security tradeoff

## Implementation Notes

This intentionally weakens security for air-gapped or development environments. The warning must be conspicuous because a silent bypass would be a security vulnerability.

Skip logic:
```bash
if [[ "$*" == *"--skip-checksum"* ]] || [[ "$NEEDLE_SKIP_CHECKSUM" == "1" ]]; then
  echo >&2 "WARNING: Checksum verification disabled. Installing without verification is a security risk."
  SKIP_CHECKSUM=1
fi
```

Prerequisites: Depends on checksum verification core logic being implemented (second child bead).
issue.title: Add explicit opt-out mechanism with warning

issue.description:
Found during the ADR-002 field-guide independent review (2026-08-12). NOT previously recorded; discovered while auditing the full flush/restore path.

Reproduced with bead 0.1.1 in disposable workspaces:
  source: 2 issues, 3 labels, 1 blocks edge, 1 issue_data namespace, 1 external_reference, 2 events
  bead sync flush-only, then bead sync import-only --input CP --restore-into-empty --actor X
  restored: labels 3 OK, dependencies 1 OK, events 2 OK, issue_data 0 LOST, external_references 0 LOST, revision 3 -> 1 LOST

The checkpoint contains only issue and event record types. Labels and dependencies survive because they are carried inline as members of the issue record. There is no record type for external references and no member for them on the issue record, so every (namespace, key, value) written through bead ref add is destroyed by a flush/restore cycle.

WHY THIS IS THE MOST SEVERE OF THE ROUND-TRIP LOSSES: research/specs/native-field-guide-v1.md L168-170 and L213 make external references THE public mechanism binding rehydrated beads back to their source tracker IDs. The same document's rehearsal procedure flushes a checkpoint and restores it into a fresh workspace. As implemented, that rehearsal silently destroys the entire traceability chain it exists to prove.

Fix: carry external references in the checkpoint (either as an inline issue member alongside labels/dependencies, or as a distinct record_type) and write them on both import paths. Add round-trip coverage - see the conformance-test bead.

Round-3 review (2026-08-13): the restore path is genuinely fixed and this bead is correctly closed — a flush/restore-into-empty round trip on a build of e5141b9 preserved external references 1 -> 1. However the fix commit 9836b07 relocated the loss to the merge path: reconcile_and_merge now DELETEs external_references and reinserts only what the incoming record carries, so merging any checkpoint without the member (including every checkpoint released 0.1.1 can produce) empties them. Tracked as bf-1cwrc; do not treat this bead's closure as covering --merge.

issue.description:
Two `needle-ci` runs failed on iad-ci with the same signature, 9h and 11h
before 2026-08-06 12:35Z:

- `needle-ci-vnmhd` — workflow message "Max duration limit exceeded",
  node exit **101**
- `needle-ci-x2wx2` — identical

Exit 101 is the Rust convention for a panic / `cargo test` failure, so this
is a real red suite, not just the duration cap. The duration message means
the run also hit the workflow's max-duration before finishing.

Relates to the epic bf-21tze ("cut NEEDLE CI from a ~50min red run to a
<10min green run") — this bead records the concrete current failure so the
epic has a reproducible starting point rather than a general description.

## Also observed: needle-ci pile-up

At 12:35Z there were **four** needle-ci workflows queued simultaneously
(`needle-ci-8x2jj` 76m, `-f46kr` 69m, `-kz4qz` 62m, `-xt8tz` 62m), none of
them able to schedule a pod. Each push spawns another run while the previous
ones are still queued, so the queue grows faster than it drains. Consider a
concurrency limit / `synchronization` semaphore on the needle-ci template so
only one run is in flight per branch.

## Reproducing

Pod logs are gone (`podGC: OnPodCompletion`). Resubmit with a
`podGC: OnWorkflowCompletion` override, or stream logs while running.

issue.description:
Found 2026-08-02 upgrading ex44 to v0.2.16.

'needle upgrade' downloaded 0.2.16, ran canary validation, scored 0/4 and
rejected the binary. The rejection is NOT a regression in the new build — the
canary expectations under ~/.needle/canary/expected/ are dated 2026-03-21 and
have not tracked bead-forge's vocabulary since.

expected/canary-bzl.yaml (the happy-path test) asserts:

    final_status: done

bead-forge has no 'done' status. Statuses actually in use across real
workspaces are: open, in_progress, blocked, closed, completed, pending, ready.
A closed bead reports 'closed'. NEEDLE knows this — src/types/mod.rs carries the
comment "br show --json emits 'closed' for done beads. Treat as equivalent".
So canary-bzl is unsatisfiable by ANY needle binary, old or new, and the canary
gate can never pass.

The observed run looked behaviourally fine: canary-bzl closed, canary-nnw
closed, canary-8ej blocked, canary-atw in_progress. All four were still scored
as failures, so the other three expectations are likely stale in the same way
(canary-8ej wants final_status 'open' plus a 'failure-count:1' label;
canary-nnw wants 'open' for a timeout).

Impact: the upgrade path on any host with a canary workspace is permanently
blocked, and the failure presents as 'the new binary is bad' rather than 'the
test fixtures rotted'. bench has no canary workspace, so it promoted 0.2.16
straight to :stable and its workers hot-reloaded correctly — good evidence the
binary itself is fine.

Not urgent for correctness on ex44: it still has the deprecated br shim at
~/.local/bin/br, so its 0.2.14 workers' 'br close' continues to work. The cost
is that ex44 stays on old binaries.

Fix direction: refresh the four expected/*.yaml against current bead-forge
vocabulary, and add an assertion that each expected final_status is a status
bf can actually produce, so this rots loudly next time. Also surface per-test
detail — 'needle canary --status' only prints channel state, giving no clue
which expectation failed or why.

Acceptance: 'needle upgrade' on ex44 passes canary and promotes to :stable.
issue.notes:
[migrated comment from bf-5my6q, 2026-08-02T19:53:30.387684238Z, author cli]
Fuller diagnosis 2026-08-02 — NOT a fixture-only fix. Five independent defects; the gate has almost certainly never worked.

1. NO BEAD RESET. CanaryRunner::run() has no reset/seed step — grep for reset_bead/seed/set_status in src/canary/mod.rs returns nothing. The four beads keep whatever terminal state the last run left (now: canary-bzl=closed, canary-nnw=closed, canary-8ej=blocked, canary-atw=in_progress). A worker cannot claim a closed bead, so later runs do nothing.

2. RACE. run_test() spawns `needle run --workspace ... --count 1` WITHOUT NEEDLE_INNER=1. That form detaches into tmux and returns immediately — the upgrade output prints "Started worker ... in tmux session / Attach with: tmux attach -t ...". So child.try_wait() returns exit 0 within milliseconds and get_actual_outcome() reads the bead long before any agent work. The exit code compared for Success/Failure is the launcher's, not the agent's.

3. StateMachine UNIMPLEMENTED. get_actual_outcome() hardcodes state_transitions: Vec::new() ("Not tracked in basic canary tests"). outcomes_match() does transitions.iter().all(|t| actual.state_transitions.contains(t)); against an always-empty vec any non-empty expected list is unsatisfiable. canary-atw could only pass with zero transitions, i.e. vacuously.

4. STALE VOCABULARY. ExpectedOutcome::default_final_status() returns "done", and expected/canary-bzl.yaml asserts final_status: done. bead-forge has no 'done' status (open/in_progress/blocked/closed/completed/pending/ready). The rot is in the source default too, so omitting the field does not help.

5. USES br. get_actual_outcome() runs Command::new(&self.br_path).args(["show", id, "--json"]). On a host without the deprecated br shim the canary errors instead of validating — same root cause as bf-15tys.

Consequence: the canary cannot pass for ANY binary, which is why 'needle upgrade' on ex44 rejected v0.2.16 at 0/4. Nothing is wrong with that build — bench has no canary workspace, promoted it, and both workers hot-reloaded and now emit 'bf close'.

Real fix spans all five points plus refreshed fixtures plus a CI cycle — materially more than editing YAML. Until then the gate protects nothing; it is a permanent block that presents as "the new binary is bad".
issue.title: Canary expectations are stale (expect status 'done'), so every upgrade is rejected 0/4 on ex44

issue.close_reason: Investigation complete. Root cause identified: Resolve strand spawns claude processes without setting working directory in src/strand/resolve.rs:333. When supervisor starts from $HOME, workers inherit $HOME, and Resolve-spawned claude processes get cwd=$HOME. The strand is not currently in the active waterfall, but was active during the 2026-07-29 incident. Processes hung for 11-13 hours without being reaped. Fix: add .current_dir(workspace) to Command::new("claude") call. Bead updated with full technical analysis.
issue.description:
Observed 2026-07-29 ~13:35 EDT on lab (100.81.129.38): load average 304-308 on a 12-core box (worse than any prior recorded fleet incident, including the 07-28 17-pinned-worker crisis that peaked at load 200+). vmstat confirmed it was real, not cosmetic: procs.r (runnable) was 281-295, %sy (kernel time) pegged at 100%, %us at 0% — pure context-switch thrashing (70-100k switches/sec), not actual work. Memory/swap were fine (34/62Gi used, 254Mi swap) — ruled out memory pressure as the driver.

Root cause of the load: found via `ps -eo comm --no-headers | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn` — 115 separate 'claude' processes, vastly more than the 4 live 'needle run' supervisors present at the time, and far beyond any previously recorded fleet size. Per-process inspection (`readlink /proc/<pid>/cwd`) showed EVERY one of the 115 had cwd = /home/coding — the bare home directory, not any project repo/workspace. Elapsed times ranged 41735-48134s (11.6-13.4h), clustered into groups sharing identical spawn timestamps (consistent with programmatic mass-spawn over time, not 115 separate manual terminal sessions). All 115 shared PPID = the tmux server hosting the needle-supervisor session (normal tmux pane-reparenting, not itself meaningful).

IMPORTANT — this is distinct from bf-12bim (supervisor zombie/defunct-child non-reaping, GH #12): these were LIVE, RUNNING processes, not <defunct> zombies. Proof: `pkill -9 -x claude` successfully killed all of them immediately (zombies are already dead and cannot be re-killed) — pgrep -c -x claude went to 0/1, then within seconds needle supervise's autoscaler correctly spun up 3 fresh workers with correct cwd (~/claude-print, ~/miroir, ~/drawrace), confirming the supervisor's spawn/autoscale logic itself is healthy. run-queue and load recovered immediately (vmstat procs.r dropped to 1-3, idle% to 82%, free memory 4.7Gi -> 24Gi).

NOT YET ROOT-CAUSED — open research questions for whoever picks this up:
1. What code path spawns a 'claude' process with cwd left at the operator's home directory instead of cd'ing into the target workspace first? Check src/dispatch/mod.rs (run_process) and src/supervisor/mod.rs (spawn_worker) for any fallback/default path taken when workspace resolution fails, is empty, or a workspace arg is omitted — does it silently fall back to the process's inherited cwd instead of erroring?
2. Why did ~115 of these accumulate over ~11-13h without anything reaping/killing them? Is there a retry loop that spawns a new claude on every tick without checking/killing the previous attempt if it hasn't exited? Cross-check against bf-1ynu9 (supervisor spawns workers via current_exe() instead of PATH lookup) and bf-12bim (zombie reaping) for any shared code path, though neither obviously explains a home-dir cwd.
3. What were these processes actually doing/blocked on for 11+ hours? If any `~/.needle/logs/needle-*.stderr.log` or claude-side transcript/session logs exist for PIDs active in the 2026-07-29 ~00:48-13:35 EDT window, check whether they show a real dispatch attempt that hung (e.g. waiting on stdin, a broken PTY, a network call that never returns) versus something spawned outside the normal dispatch path entirely (health check, canary, some other subprocess call to the 'claude' binary).

When supervisor starts from $HOME, workers inherit $HOME, and Resolve-strand-spawned claude processes get cwd=$HOME. 

Key findings:
1. ROOT CAUSE: resolve.rs invoke_resolver() spawns claude without setting cwd
2. NOT CURRENTLY ACTIVE: ResolveStrand is NOT in the active strand waterfall (StrandRunner::from_config only includes: Pluck, Mend, Explore, Weave, Unravel, Pulse, Reflect, Splice, Knot)

issue.close_reason: Implemented set_resource on all four resilient OTLP exporter wrappers (ResilientGrpcSpanExporter, ResilientHttpSpanExporter, ResilientGrpcLogExporter, ResilientHttpLogExporter). Each wrapper now delegates set_resource calls to the inner exporter via Arc::get_mut, with WARN logging if the Arc is not unique. This fixes the root cause where resource attributes (service.name, service.version, service.instance.id, deployment.cluster, needle.worker.pool) were not reaching the collector. Commit 922dd47 pushed to main.
issue.description:
## Evidence

Raw capture of the deployed needle 0.3.1 binary POSTing to /v1/logs (isolated
HOME, throwaway workspace, compression: none, local receiver) contains NO
resource attributes at all. Every string in the 598-byte payload:

  needle | INFO | {"version":"0.3.1","worker_name":"otelprobe"}
  event_type | worker.booting | worker_id | claude-code-glm-4.7-otelprobe
  session_id | de7fb055 | sequence | event_type | init.step.started | duration_ms

No service.name, no service.version, no deployment.cluster, no
needle.worker.pool, none of needle.agent/needle.model/needle.workspace.

Live dashboard (/api/dashboard, 2026-08-16 04:40 UTC) consequently shows
repo=null, semver=null, worker_pool="default" for EVERY worker in the fleet.
environment is the only field that works, and it is the one field NEEDLE does
not supply — the collector upserts deployment.cluster itself.

## Root cause

opentelemetry_sdk 0.31 pushes the Resource down the chain at provider-build time:
  SdkLoggerProvider::build() -> processor.set_resource()  (logs/logger_provider.rs:267)
  BatchLogProcessor::set_resource() -> BatchMessage::SetResource  (logs/batch_log_processor.rs:323)
  batch worker -> exporter.set_resource()

LogExporter::set_resource (logs/export.rs:153) and SpanExporter::set_resource
(trace/export.rs:74) are DEFAULTED NO-OPS on the SDK traits. src/telemetry/otlp.rs
interposes four wrappers that implement export() and nothing else:

  ResilientHttpLogExporter   (otlp.rs:306)
  ResilientGrpcLogExporter   (otlp.rs:249)
  ResilientHttpSpanExporter  (otlp.rs:192)
  ResilientGrpcSpanExporter  (otlp.rs:135)

Each inherits the no-op, absorbs the Resource, and never forwards it to the
inner opentelemetry_otlp exporter, which then serializes with its default empty
Resource. OtlpSink::build_resource() (otlp.rs:719) is correct — its output is
discarded one hop before the socket.

Metrics are unaffected: MetricExporter is passed to PeriodicReader unwrapped.
That asymmetry is why the collector transform/metric_dimensions rule, which
reads resource.attributes[...], was written against a resource that exists.

Traces to Tempo have the same defect: every NEEDLE span currently arrives with
an empty Resource.

## Deliverables

- Implement set_resource on all four wrappers, delegating to the inner exporter.
  The wrappers hold inner: Arc<...>; the SDK calls set_resource at
  provider-build time while the Arc is still unique, so Arc::get_mut is the
  delegation mechanism. WARN (do not silently continue) if the unique reference
  cannot be obtained.
- Adopt the rule in code review: a wrapper interposed on an OTel SDK exporter
  trait must implement EVERY method of that trait, including defaulted no-ops.

## Acceptance

- A raw OTLP payload captured from a real needle binary contains service.name,
  service.version, service.instance.id, and the operator-supplied
  resource_attributes (deployment.cluster, needle.worker.pool).
- Verified on the wire, not by asserting on build_resource()return value —
  that is how needle-501aa991 was closed while the dashboard stayed blank.

See docs/adr/016-otlp-resource-propagation-and-roaming-worker-identity.md and
plan.md Phase 17 (17.1).
issue.title: OTLP resilient exporter wrappers swallow set_resource — zero resource attributes reach the collector

Implements ADR-005 in docs/adr/ (005-unify...) referenced from plan.md Phase 9.

Today perform_upgrade() (src/upgrade/mod.rs) downloads a new GitHub release and overwrites
env::current_exe() directly, with zero canary validation and zero fleet propagation. Separately,
check_auto_canary()/check_hot_reload() in src/worker/mod.rs already implement a full, tested,
canary-gated hot-reload pipeline that runs every worker-loop cycle -- but it only ever reacts to
a needle-testing binary written by the (disabled) self-modification pipeline. Nothing connects
"new GitHub release" to that channel. Live-confirmed drift during 2026-07-20 audit: ex44's
installed needle reported 0.2.11 while GitHub's latest release was v0.2.12, published the same day.

Deliverables:
1. New function alongside check_for_update() (src/upgrade/mod.rs) that downloads a newer release
   to needle_home/bin/needle-testing instead of overwriting the running binary. Skip (log why) if
   a :testing binary is already present and unpromoted, so this can't clobber an in-flight
   self-modification candidate.
2. Periodic poll in needle supervise (src/supervisor/mod.rs) calling that function on interval
   supervisor.update_check_interval_secs (default 21600), gated behind new
   supervisor.auto_upgrade_check: bool (default false).
3. No changes needed to check_auto_canary()/check_hot_reload() -- verify via test that a
   release-sourced :testing binary is picked up identically to a self-modification-sourced one.
4. Regression tests per plan.md Phase 9.4.

Acceptance criteria: with auto_upgrade_check=true and a mocked newer release, a full poll cycle
produces a promoted :stable and a subsequent hot-reload in worker-loop tests; a failing canary
leaves :stable untouched; needle upgrade (manual path) is unchanged.

issue.description:
## Symptom

`cargo test --lib` never completes in CI. Measured on needle-ci-rel050-hqmbt
(2026-08-24): the check held from 12:21:41Z to 14:41:32Z -- 2h20m against its
own 900s cap -- until the verify pod hit activeDeadlineSeconds and was
SIGKILLed. No needle-ci run has succeeded in the retained window, so NO
RELEASE CAN BE CUT. v0.5.0 is blocked behind this, and 126 commits remain
unreleased including the P0 short-SHA worker panic fix (needle-161e49b7),
which the ex44 fleet is actively crash-looping on.

## Evidence (live, from the verify pod)

The lib test binary idles -- it is hung, not slow:

  CPU 15m (1.5% of one core), MEM 2616Mi

  tid=10479 [S] needle-953edf91  wchan=futex_wait_queue   <- main, awaiting tests
  tid=15015 [S] worker::tests::  wchan=futex_wait_queue
  tid=15017 [S] tokio-rt-worker  wchan=ep_poll
  tid=15030 [S] heartbeat-reloa  wchan=hrtimer_nanosleep

Two zombie `echo` processes are parented to it (ppid=10479) -- spawned and
never reaped.

## Prime suspect

`full_cycle_with_echo_agent()` (src/worker/mod.rs:8409) is the only site in
src/worker/ that sets `agent_cli: "echo"`, matching the zombies. It is one of
only three worker tests that `await worker.run()` (mod.rs:6983, 7093, 8458).

It is explicitly written to finish fast -- `IdleAction::Exit`, hot_reload
disabled, explore disabled, `agent.timeout = 5` -- so `run()` failing to
return under a MockStore is the defect. Confirm which of the three hangs
before fixing; attribution is strong but circumstantial (thread names are
truncated to `worker::tests::`).

This may be a real defect in the run loop's termination path rather than
test-only: `IdleAction::Exit` not being honoured would matter in production.

## Related, already fixed -- do not conflate

- 3cdb247 fixed the CI-side masking: `run_check` deadlocked because
  `output=$(...)` waits for every writer to close the pipe, and a
  SIGTERM-catching test binary orphaned past its cap kept fd 1/2 open. That
  made all per-target caps inert and hid this hang behind "Pod was active on
  the node longer than the specified deadline" for ~36 runs over 35h. With it,
  verify now fails in ~15 min naming the hung target. It does NOT fix this.
- The template comment blames 2026-08-17/18 hangs on CPU oversubscription,
  "fixed" with CARGO_BUILD_JOBS/RUST_TEST_THREADS=3. Same signature (a test
  left running with no completion line) -- that was likely this bug,
  misattributed.

## Acceptance criteria

- `cargo test --lib` completes locally and in needle-ci well within 900s
- The hanging test is identified by name and its root cause stated
- If `run()` can fail to honour IdleAction::Exit outside tests, that is fixed
  or filed separately with rationale
- A needle-ci run reaches the release stage
issue.notes:
## CONFIRMED 2026-08-24 by needle-ci-diag-k75vd (first run after the 3cdb247 CI fix)

The fix made the gate diagnostic: all 9 checks ran (39 min) instead of hanging
on the 4th forever (150 min). Orphans were reaped in-flight ("reaped orphaned
pid 10574/16704"), and both test targets returned exit 124 at their caps.

It is NOT one test. Seven hang, and they cluster hard:

  worker::tests::handle_exhausted_with_exit_returns_stopped
  worker::tests::handle_exhausted_with_wait_returns_selecting
  worker::tests::full_cycle_with_echo_agent
  worker::tests::config_reload_requested_mid_dispatch_waits_for_cycle_boundary
  debug_worker_hang                        (tests/integration_tests.rs)
  end_to_end_single_bead_success           (tests/integration_tests.rs)
  end_to_end_worker_loops_to_next_bead     (tests/integration_tests.rs)

## Sharpened hypothesis: the run loop never reaches a terminal state

The two `handle_exhausted_*` tests exercise the Exhausted/IdleAction path
directly, and `full_cycle_with_echo_agent` asserts exactly that outcome
(`WorkerState::Stopped || WorkerState::Exhausted`). Every hanging test is a
run-loop / exhaustion / dispatch-cycle test; no test outside that cluster
hangs. So this is very likely ONE defect in the terminal-state transition,
not seven independent ones -- fix the loop and all seven should clear.

`IdleAction::Exit` not being honoured is a PRODUCTION concern, not just a test
concern: it is the setting that lets a worker exit cleanly when out of work.
Worth checking against the claim-leak work (needle-claim-leak / outcome
postcondition beads) -- a worker that cannot reach a terminal state is a
plausible contributor to claims never being released.

Start with `debug_worker_hang` -- the name says someone has been here before.

## Separately revealed by the same run (NOT this bead)

"installer tests: exit code 1" also fails. It was invisible before, because the
old run_check hung on cargo test --lib and never reached it. Needs its own bead.
issue.title: worker::tests hangs forever in worker.run(), blocking every needle-ci release

[migrated labels from bf-1993c]
split-child

## Remediation plan for needle-ci test failures (2026-08-23)

Builds on the RCA (needle-e6640f66). Every claim was re-verified against HEAD (0552c4a) today. Deltas since the RCA: (1) the shared tree compiles again — `cargo check --lib` clean in 7s (incremental); the E0428/E0599 breakage from concurrent workers settled; (2) RCA cluster E ("undiagnosed") is now DIAGNOSED — I ran the two config tests locally (pure in-memory unit tests; no store/Explore involvement); (3) CI still red: Failed runs through needle-ci-qwwkt (09:34Z), 5vbdg + nbnnr in flight at ~10:40Z.

### Sharpened finding — cluster A hides a production bug, not just stale tests

`prepare_release_events` (outcome/mod.rs:102-159) is flush-only and never emits `BeadReleased`. Five sites then compute `release_succeeded = events.any(BeadReleased)` from events that cannot contain it — outcome/mod.rs:528 and :546 (orphaned / no-shipped-work), :708 (gate failure), :786 (handle_failure), :853 (handle_timeout). Live consequences:

1. `increment_failure_count` never runs on Failure/Timeout/GateFailure/Orphaned paths → `failure-count:N` labels never written.
2. Quarantine ceiling (`outcome.quarantine_after_failures`, default 5) never enforced → beads can re-claim-and-fail forever — the exact 2026-08-17 incident shape (needle-3386daef) the regression test memorializes.
3. `deferred` label never added on Timeout (it sits inside the dead branch, outcome/mod.rs:856-884).
4. Mitosis `repeat_interval` re-split never triggers — src/mitosis/mod.rs:836 reads the same `failure-count:` labels.

`handle_failure` pushes a fallback `BeadReleased` for telemetry AFTER the check (:823-834) — which is why telemetry looks healthy downstream while the behavior is dead. Fixing the tests without fixing this would bake the bug in.

---

### R1 — P0 — Restore release-accounting (the production bug). Effort: M (0.5-1 day)

Design decision required; three variants:

- **R1a (RECOMMENDED): decouple accounting from release telemetry.** Handlers increment the failure count and evaluate quarantine from the OUTCOME classification alone (Failure / Timeout / GateFailure / Orphaned-no-work), delete every `release_succeeded` gate, and make `handle_timeout` add the `deferred` label unconditionally. `BeadReleased` telemetry becomes an intent event emitted where the action is decided (or definitively by `Worker::apply_bead_action`). Steps: (1) remove the five `release_succeeded` blocks, calling `increment_failure_count` + threshold check directly; (2) consolidate the orphan-path increments (:528/:546) into the same helper to guarantee one accounting site per outcome; (3) move the fallback `BeadReleased` push ahead of nothing — emit it at decision time in every releasing handler; (4) update the six behavioral outcome tests (failure-count, quarantine-at-threshold, timeout-deferred) to the new contract.
  Why: release success is no longer knowable at handler time under the single-mutation-point design, and a failed release should not erase failure accounting — a bead that failed AND failed to release is a worse state, not a reset.
- **R1b: move increment/quarantine into `Worker::apply_bead_action` (worker/mod.rs:3484).** Purest mutation discipline, but scatters outcome policy into the worker and forces every handler test onto a worker-level harness — larger migration, blurs the handler contract the refactor created.
- **R1c: make `prepare_release_events` emit `BeadReleased` again.** Smallest diff, but re-introduces the telemetry lie (event claims a release that hasn't happened / may fail) the refactor removed. Reject.

Risks / side effects (R1a): behavior ACTIVATES — beads currently looping will start quarantining at 5 failures (desired; operator-visible: monitor `BeadQuarantined` telemetry post-rollout, and confirm a workflow exists to unblock quarantined beads); mitosis `repeat_interval` re-splits start firing (verify its default); double-increment risk if any accounting site is missed in the consolidation; touches outcome/mod.rs which concurrent workers also edit — serialize via a dedicated bead with blocking deps (see sequencing).

### R2 — P0 — Migrate the 12 stale cluster-A tests to the BeadAction contract. Effort: S-M (0.5 day)

Steps: (1) for each outcome test asserting `store.actions()` contains `StoreAction::Release` after `handler.handle()` alone — structurally impossible since 96e691e/75f1257 moved `store.release()` into `apply_bead_action` — assert `result.bead_action == BeadAction::Released` instead, keeping at least one end-to-end assert per handler category by applying the action through a worker harness; (2) in `regression_2026_08_17_exit_zero_without_close_cannot_loop` (worker/mod.rs:6951), move the two store-status asserts (`released.status == Open`, `assignee == None`) to AFTER `worker.apply_bead_action(action)` — they currently assert pre-refactor ordering; the later "recovered" asserts are already post-apply and fine.
Risks: assertion weakening if tests only check the returned action (mitigate as above — worker-level regression tests at worker/mod.rs:6883/:7830/:7849 already cover the apply path); merge conflicts with concurrent outcome/mod.rs edits — land R1+R2 as ONE bead.

### R3 — P1 — worker_config message contract (2 failures). Effort: XS (30 min)

The reason string says "without supervisor supervision" (worker_config.rs:93); tests assert `.contains("no supervisor")` at :116, :141, :185, and the doc example at :76 repeats it. Steps: keep the code's message (it is the more informative one), fix the three asserts + doc example to a stable substring ("without supervisor supervision"), and prefer asserting on a `const` reason fragment exported next to the validator so string and test cannot drift again. Check whether the doc block is a compiled doctest; if so it must match or `cargo test --doc` breaks next.
Risks: none meaningful.

### R4 — P1 — mend key-space unification + idle-worker policy decision (2 failures). Effort: M (0.5-1 day)

Verified: `worker_current_beads` is keyed by `hb.qualified_id` (mend.rs:460-468, bare fallback only when empty) while beads carry bare assignees, so the lookup at :505 misses and falls to the registry check → different-bead clearing (:509-512) is unreachable for bare assignees — same shape as the 583-stuck-bead incident (needle-44e7e5cd). Separately, `open_bead_with_idle_worker_assignee_cleared` contradicts the deliberate keep-policy ("Don't clear - they may resume work", :513-519).
Steps: (1) build a reverse alias when scanning heartbeats — insert both the qualified key and the bare worker name — so lookups hit for either key space; (2) make the explicit policy call for idle-live workers: RECOMMEND keep-with-age-cutoff (keep while the heartbeat is fresh; clear once the claim exceeds the existing stale-by-age limit, mend.rs:~176) — this honors the resume-work intent while bounding stuck time, and gives the idle test a meaningful aged-fixture form; (3) rewrite both tests to encode the decided policy.
Risks: over-clearing → duplicate work / starvation churn; under-clearing → persistent stuck beads (both have incident history); mitigation: validate the new logic against a copy of a live store before fleet rollout, and watch mend telemetry for clear-rate anomalies.

### R5 — P1 — resolve test hermeticity (1 failure). Effort: S (1-2 h)

Verified: `invoke_resolve_agent` spawns real `claude` (resolve/mod.rs:575); on CI the binary is absent so the spawn errors instead of timing out. Steps: make the binary injectable (config field, default "claude"), point the test at a committed fixture script that sleeps past the 100ms timeout, assert the timeout message. Skip-if-absent is the weaker fallback (still env-dependent). Reuse the hermetic-probe pattern already established for PATH-probing tests (set_hermetic_probe_path).
Risks: small config-surface addition; ensure the fixture keeps its exec bit in git.

### R6 — P1 — the two config tests (DIAGNOSED today; was RCA cluster E). Effort: XS (30 min)

- `test_otlp_config_matches_plan_md` (config/mod.rs:11754): plan.md's telemetry snippet uses field `otlp`; the implemented schema expects `otlp_sink` (siblings: `file_sink`, `stdout_sink`, `hooks`). The test is the plan-sync guard working AS DESIGNED — fix docs/plan/plan.md's telemetry example to the current schema. Code is the source of truth here (schema is implemented and live).
- `changed_sections_detects_multiple_section_changes` (config/mod.rs:12030): `limits.providers` defaults to an EMPTY map, so `.clear()` is a no-op — only 2 of 3 sections differ and `len() >= 3` fails at :12041. Born-broken fixture. Fix: seed `config1.limits.providers` with an entry (agent.timeout 3600→999 and the telemetry flip are already real changes), then tighten to assert the exact set {agent, telemetry, limits}.
Risks: none. NOTE: another worker currently has uncommitted edits in src/config/mod.rs — coordinate before touching it.

### R7a — P0 (visibility) — CI lane + memory. Effort: S (half day incl. verification)

The meta-failures that masked diagnosis are still live. Steps: (1) scripts/definition-of-done.sh:123-131 — per-lane `timeout 900` is below lib-lane reality (~500s compile + ~400s tests). Preferred: split build from run (`cargo test --lib --no-run` once, then per-suite runs with 600s each) so red detection stays fast; minimum: raise to 1800. (2) declarative-config needle-ci-builder-workflowtemplate.yml: the verify container's 2Gi memory request caused a node-pressure eviction at ~3.5Gi observed usage — raise the request to 4Gi (limit is already 4Gi; request=limit stops eviction).
Risks: larger request reduces schedulability (check node capacity before merging); longer timeouts slow red-signal (avoided by the build/run split).

### R7b — P2 — stop compile-broken pushes. Effort: S

Steps: add an incremental `cargo check` to the per-bead verification commands (config-level; docs/configuration.md documents the verification list) so a worker's own gate catches a broken tree BEFORE push; keep the DoD failure summary as-is (100-line tail since 4c055c9 is adequate) or switch to `--format terse` + failures list for completeness.
Risks: adds seconds-to-a-minute per bead; residual race remains (tree can break between check and push) — R8 is the real mitigation.

### R8 — P2 — concurrent-worker discipline. Effort: continuous (process)

The RCA documented two broken-push windows from concurrent workers on the shared checkout. Mitigations that fit the existing model: blocking deps between beads touching the same files (never leave two simultaneously-ready beads over outcome/mod.rs), pathspec-precise staging (established practice), and evaluating whether the existing `.needle-predispatch-sha` drift check can refuse dispatch when HEAD moved under an in-flight bead.

---

### Recommended sequencing

- **Wave 0 (hours, parallel-safe — disjoint files):** R3 + R6 (one bead: worker_config.rs, config tests, plan.md) ‖ R7a (DoD script + declarative-config). Removes 4 of 20 failures and makes CI signal trustworthy — do this FIRST so every later wave verifies against real signal.
- **Wave 1 (day 1-2, single serialized bead):** R1a + R2 together — one contract change plus its test migration; must not be split across concurrent workers (same file, same claim hazard as the 2026-08-09 commitgraph duplicate).
- **Wave 2:** R4 (mend.rs) ‖ R5 (resolve/mod.rs + fixture).
- **Continuous:** R7b, R8.

Total: ~3-4 focused worker-days. Wave 0 ≈ half a day.

### Global risks

- Concurrent-worker interference throughout (mitigate: the wave structure + bead-level blocking deps above).
- R1 activates dormant fleet behavior (quarantine, mitosis re-split) — flag in the rollout commit and watch telemetry for the first fleet cycles.
- Every implementer bead closes only on a green needle-ci run (existing DoD rule); with ~20 red tests, Wave 0 must land before anything can close on green — another reason it goes first.

### For the downstream bead

needle-1c47d3ee ("Investigate current test setup and environment") is largely subsumed by the RCA + this plan; recommend closing it as absorbed, or narrowing it to executing/verifying R7a only.

### Acceptance-criteria mapping

≥3 options: R1(a/b/c) + R2-R8, eight distinct remediations with a rejected-alternative analysis inside R1. Steps: per option. Prioritized with rationale: P0 = R1/R2 (13 failures + live production defect) and R7a (CI signal trustworthiness gates all verification); P1 = R3/R4/R5/R6 (independent deterministic clusters, small); P2 = R7b/R8 (prevention). Risks/side effects: per option + global section. Effort: XS→M per option, ~3-4 days total.

issue.description:
## Problem

When agent.routing.rules is configured but no rule matches the active model, NEEDLE silently falls back to agent.default (or routing.default_adapter if set). This means a misconfigured or unrecognized model (e.g. a new provider, a typo, a model removed from the adapter list) routes silently to the wrong adapter with no signal to the operator.

## What to add

Add an optional boolean agent.routing.strict (default: false):

  agent:
    routing:
      strict: true
      rules:
        - match_model: "(claude-)?(sonnet|opus|fable|haiku).*"
          adapter: claude-print
        - match_model: "glm.*"
          adapter: claude-code-glm-4.7

When strict: true and no rule matches the active model:
1. Do NOT fall back to agent.default or routing.default_adapter.
2. Emit a RoutingFailed telemetry event with the model name and rule count.
3. Return Err from apply_routing_rules with a clear human-readable message:
   "no routing rule matched model 'gpt-4o' — add a rule to agent.routing.rules or set routing.strict: false to fall back to the default adapter"
4. Propagates through resolve_adapter -> dispatch -> marks the bead as failed (not orphaned), surfaced in the bead list.

## Schema changes

pub struct RoutingConfig {
    pub rules: Vec<RoutingRule>,
    pub default_adapter: Option<String>,
    pub strict: bool,  // new, default false
}

Add RoutingFailed to EventKind:
RoutingFailed {
    bead_id: BeadId,
    model: String,
    rules_tried: usize,
}

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] RoutingConfig has strict: bool (default false); existing configs without strict behave unchanged.
- [ ] strict: true + no match: apply_routing_rules returns Err with the message above; RoutingFailed telemetry emitted.
- [ ] strict: false + no match: existing fallback behavior unchanged.
- [ ] Bead is marked failed (dispatch error), not orphaned or silently retried.
- [ ] Unit tests: strict=true no-match -> Err; strict=false no-match -> default; strict=true match -> Ok.
- [ ] cargo test passes (push and wait for needle-ci).
issue.title: routing: strict mode — fail loudly when no rule matches an unrecognized model

issue.description:
The starvation detector files a fresh bead every time it fires. Three identical beads existed as of 2026-08-12 — bf-1o1sr (total beads 190), bf-61qvt (191), bf-8rep6 (192) — differing only in the bead count in the body. Left alone this accumulates one bead per occurrence forever, and each one is itself an open bead that inflates the count the next alert reports.

Fix: dedupe on firing. Either (a) find an existing open starvation bead for the same workspace and append a comment instead of creating, or (b) attach a stable dedup key (label 'alert:starvation:<workspace>') and skip creation when one is already open.

Context: these alerts were NOT spurious. 'Open beads exist but Pluck found none' was correct — the dependency graph had 10 beads stuck at status=blocked with no blockers, 21 inverted verify-blocks-build edges, and a 5-node cycle, so pluckable work was scarce while open beads existed. Graph repaired 2026-08-12; if the alert keeps firing after that, re-triage.

Changed from substring matching `args[0].contains("/needle")` to strict basename matching: extract basename from argv[0] path, require it is exactly "needle", and require argv[1] == "run" (after skipping NEEDLE_INNER=1 prefix). This eliminates false positives from child processes with .needle/ paths, needle-transform-claude binaries, and unrelated orphaned processes. Fix committed and pushed as 648a541.
issue.description:
needle status's process-table scan for "unregistered needle run processes" produces massive false-positive counts (93 on ex44, 29 on lab, confirmed 2026-08-13) that do not correspond to real unregistered workers.

Root cause (verified via ps/proc inspection of the flagged PIDs):

1. Child processes of ALREADY-REGISTERED workers get swept in as if they were separate top-level workers. Each registered worker's per-bead pipeline (`bash -c cd <repo> && git rev-parse HEAD > .needle/... `, `claude --print --verbose ...`, `cat`, the `needle-transform-claude` output-piping helper) contains the substring "needle" somewhere in its cmdline (a `.needle/` path or the `needle-transform-claude` binary name), which appears to be enough to match the scanner's heuristic. These are not independent workers — they're already accounted for under their parent's registered identifier.

2. Some flagged PIDs have NO relation to needle at all — orphaned pytest runs, shell scripts (e.g. poll-oauth-usage.sh), an idle `uv run uvicorn` server, stray `sleep` calls, all reparented to PID 1. These appear to be swept in by the scanner walking orphaned (PPID=1) process trees generally, not by any needle-specific match.

Verified by cross-checking against a strict argv match for actual `needle run` invocations (`/needle run --workspace ...`) — that count matches the registered-worker count exactly (12 on ex44, 6 on lab), confirming the fleet itself is healthy and the discrepancy is entirely in the status detector.

Fix should make the "discovered worker" process-table scan match only genuine `needle run` invocations (argv0 resolves to the needle binary AND argv1 == "run"), not any process whose cmdline merely contains the substring "needle", and should not treat arbitrary orphaned process trees as worker candidates.

issue.close_reason:
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED AND FIXED. build_http_providers() in src/telemetry/otlp.rs called .with_endpoint(config.endpoint.clone()) for all three OTLP HTTP exporters (traces/metrics/logs), passing the bare configured endpoint with no per-signal path. opentelemetry-otlp only auto-appends /v1/traces, /v1/metrics, /v1/logs when resolving from an OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*_ENDPOINT env var - NOT when .with_endpoint() is called programmatically, which is what NEEDLE does. Every HTTP export request has therefore always hit the collector's bare root (e.g. http://needle-otel-ex44-.../4318/) and gotten a 404, silently and permanently, for every worker that has ever run with otlp_sink.enabled=true.

Confirmed by first fixing the swallowed-error bug (the "sink flush failed: failed to flush logger provider" log line only showed Display, not the wrapped cause - fixed to show the full anyhow chain), then reproducing: the real error was reqwest::Error { kind: Status(404, None), url: ".../4318/" }. Cross-checked directly against the opentelemetry-otlp 0.31.1 crate source (vendored locally) - confirmed with_endpoint() is used verbatim with no path appended, matching the crate's own test suite behavior.

Fix (commit 40de7e3): append the correct /v1/{signal} suffix per exporter before calling with_endpoint(), trimming a trailing slash on the base endpoint first. build_grpc_providers is unaffected (gRPC has no per-signal URL paths).

Live-verified with a scoped diagnostic worker (identifier=otel-fixcheck, local debug build, workspace NEEDLE): boots clean, claims a real bead (bf-47ab9), and its full event stream (worker.booting, bead.claim.attempted/succeeded, build.heartbeat, agent.routing_decision, agent.dispatched, transform.started, worker.state_transition, rate_limit.allowed, init.step.*) is now visible on dashboard.ardenone.com/needle via direct API query - the first real (non-synthetic) worker telemetry this pipeline has ever successfully delivered end-to-end.

Also fixed in the same investigation: a fresh, unrelated compile break on main (bf-5stm4, TimeoutReason missing Display) that was blocking any local build.
issue.description:
## Problem

Confirmed live on ex44 2026-08-12: real fleet workers (rota-1, hoop-1) converted to telemetry.otlp_sink.enabled=true both boot clean (bf-3s2b0/192a2ab's crash fix holds) and hit exactly ONE "NEEDLE telemetry: sink flush failed: failed to flush logger provider" line right as the worker loop starts. That single line is the LAST OTLP-related log line either process ever produces.

Over the following ~5 minutes, both workers stayed completely healthy doing real work (heartbeat files updating every ~30s, rota-1 on bf-576h8, hoop-1 moved from bf-1sy9t to bf-qt5hn - i.e. actually completing/cycling beads), proving the worker/local file_sink telemetry path is unaffected. But queried needle-dashboard's /api/dashboard directly (via a scoped port-forward, bypassing the OAuth gate) 8 times over 160s: zero events, zero worker entries for rota-1 or hoop-1 ever appeared. active_workers stayed 0 the whole time.

By contrast, a separate synthetic curl POST straight to the collector's /v1/logs endpoint (with valid authentication) DID land and IS visible on the dashboard (worker_id=unknown, event_type=test.smoke, timestamped 06:14:04Z) - so the collector, VictoriaLogs, and dashboard side of the pipe are all confirmed working. The break is specifically in NEEDLE's own OTLP exporter: after the first flush failure, it appears to stop trying entirely rather than retrying on the next periodic flush (metrics_interval_secs=10 in this config - there should have been ~30 more flush attempts in that window if the exporter were still alive).

## Hypothesis (not confirmed - nobody has read the actual underlying error)

The "sink flush failed: failed to flush logger provider" message wraps whatever the real reqwest/tonic/opentelemetry-sdk error was, but that inner error is not logged - only the wrapper text is. Two candidate mechanisms:
1. The periodic export task (likely spawned via the same tokio::spawn pattern bf-3s2b0 just fixed for the drop-monitor task) panics or returns early on its first failure and is never restarted - a sibling bug to the one bf-3s2b0 fixed, same file/area (src/telemetry/otlp.rs), different task.
2. The BatchLogProcessor's background worker thread/task exits after an unhandled error from its export attempt, which is normal-ish behavior for some OTel SDK batch processors on certain error classes, but would mean NEEDLE needs its own retry/restart wrapper around it - the SDK default is not to silently resume.

## What to check

- Read the actual error via a debug build or by adding a Display of the underlying error to the "sink flush failed" log line (currently just "failed to flush logger provider" with no source/cause chain rendered).
- Check whether the OTLP log-export background task/thread is still alive after the first failure (thread list, tokio task count, or an explicit liveness marker).
- Check whether this is a race specific to worker startup (first flush landing before something else - e.g. the collector's receiver - is fully warmed up) vs a persistent per-connection failure (e.g. HTTP/2 connection pool issue, DNS caching a bad result once).
- Reproduce with RUST_LOG=debug or equivalent to get more detail than the current single-line warning.

## Acceptance criteria

- Root cause of the first flush failure identified (actual error text captured, not just the wrapper message).
- Fix confirmed: a worker with otlp_sink.enabled=true runs for 5+ minutes, its heartbeat/claim/dispatch events are visible on needle-dashboard's /api/dashboard without needing a synthetic/manual event to prove the pipe works.
- If the fix is "retry on transient export failure", add a regression test forcing one export failure and asserting the exporter keeps trying on subsequent flushes rather than going permanently silent.

## Context

Found while live-verifying bf-3s2b0/192a2ab (the OTLP startup-crash fix) against real fleet workers per user request. That fix is solid - crash is gone - but this is a second, distinct bug in the same area that was masked by the crash bug (nobody could get a worker to stay alive long enough with OTLP on to notice this one until now).
issue.title: OTLP export silently dies after first transient flush failure, never recovers

issue.notes:
# ETXTBSY Retry Implementation Plan

## Selected Spawn Site: src/kubectl.rs (get_workflow_phase function)

**Location:** Line 167-178 in `src/kubectl.rs`
**Risk Level:** LOW (simple, isolated, well-tested)

### Current Code

```rust
let output = Command::new("kubectl")
    .arg("--kubeconfig")
    .arg(IAD_CI_KUBECONFIG)
    .arg("get")
    .arg("workflow")
    .arg(workflow_name)
    .arg("-n")
    .arg(ns)
    .arg("-o")
    .arg("jsonpath={.status.phase}")
    .output()
    .context("failed to execute kubectl command")?;
```

### Why This Site Is Ideal

1. **Simple**: Straightforward `std::process::Command::output()` call
2. **Low risk**: Well-isolated function with comprehensive error handling
3. **Test coverage**: 700+ lines of tests in the same file
4. **No complex interaction**: Uses `.output()` not `.spawn()`, so no child process management
5. **Already has retry wrapper**: Uses `get_workflow_phase_with_retry` at higher level - ETXTBSY retry adds OS-level protection

### Implementation Changes Required

#### 1. Import the retry wrapper (add to top of file)

```rust
use crate::bead_store::spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync;
```

#### 2. Replace the Command::new(...).output() call (line 167-178)

BEFORE:
```rust
let output = Command::new("kubectl")
    .arg("--kubeconfig")
    .arg(IAD_CI_KUBECONFIG)
    // ... args ...
    .output()
    .context("failed to execute kubectl command")?;
```

AFTER:
```rust
let output = spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync(
    || {
        Command::new("kubectl")
            .arg("--kubeconfig")
            .arg(IAD_CI_KUBECONFIG)
            .arg("get")
            .arg("workflow")
            .arg(workflow_name)
            .arg("-n")
            .arg(ns)
            .arg("-o")
            .arg("jsonpath={.status.phase}")
            .output()
    },
    5,  // max_attempts
    20, // backoff_ms
)
.context("failed to execute kubectl command")?;
```

### Error Handling Adjustments

**None needed.** The existing error handling is already correct:

- Uses `.context()` to add context to errors
- Already wraps the command execution in a Result-returning function
- Higher-level retry logic (`get_workflow_phase_with_retry`) remains unchanged
- The retry wrapper preserves non-ETXTBSY errors (immediate return)

### Verification

The retry wrapper function `spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync` exists and is appropriate:

- **Location**: `src/bead_store/mod.rs:674-715`
- **Signature**: Takes a closure returning `std::io::Result<T>`, max_attempts, and backoff_ms
- **Behavior**: 
  - Returns immediately on non-ETXTBSY errors
  - Retries only on errno 26 (ETXTBSY)
  - Returns the successful output or the final ETXTBSY error
- **Compatibility**: Perfect match for `Command::output()` which returns `std::io::Result<Output>`

### Testing Strategy

The existing test suite already covers this function:

- `test_workflow_phase_from_str` - validates output parsing
- No new tests needed - retry wrapper has its own test suite in `tests/etxtbsy_retry.rs`
- Manual verification: Can trigger ETXTBSY by running `kubectl` immediately after a binary update (if ever needed)

### Rollback Plan

If issues arise, reverting is trivial:

1. Remove the `use crate::bead_store::spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync;` import
2. Restore the original `Command::new(...).output()` call
3. No other code changes needed

This site provides maximum safety for the first ETXTBSY retry integration.
issue.title: Select and document first spawn site for ETXTBSY retry

[migrated comment from bf-2fbz7, 2026-08-11T15:19:25.944217154Z, author cli]
Found 2026-08-11 during a lab incident investigation: bead bf-5vfu in the domain-check repo ("Investigate br claim exclusion logic") accumulated 973,589 events in its events list — almost entirely repeating claimed/assignee_changed pairs from a claim-race/retry loop. This inflated that single bead's JSON record to 246MB (out of a 352-bead, 247MB total .beads/issues.jsonl). The bloated file was committed 153 times, growing domain-check's .git to 4.1GB, and is a strong suspect in a series of git-process OOM kills on lab (7x, 07:32-07:55 EDT, each ~12-13GB RSS) that ultimately took the whole NEEDLE tmux fleet down.

Root gap: NEEDLE/bf never caps or prunes the per-bead events list, so any bead caught in a claim-race loop becomes a ticking git-bloat time bomb once its bead store gets committed. Checked 'bf --help' end to end — no compact/vacuum/prune-events command exists to fix this after the fact either. The 'compaction_level' field on the bead schema suggests this was anticipated but never implemented/wired up.

Could not fix bf-5vfu itself: trimming it would mean hand-editing .beads/issues.jsonl directly, which is a hard prohibition in this environment (must go through bf, never edit .beads/ by hand), and there is no bf command that does it instead.

Suggested fixes: (1) cap events-per-bead in bf/br (e.g. hard limit + oldest-N-dropped or summarized), (2) surface a bf command to compact/truncate a bead's event history, (3) NEEDLE-side: detect and circuit-break a claim-race loop before it can generate hundreds of thousands of events on one bead.
issue.title: Unbounded per-bead events list causes runaway git bloat (no compaction tool)

issue.description:
## Problem

Every adapter already declares which inference provider it uses --
`AgentAdapter.provider: Option<String>` (dispatch/mod.rs:264-266), e.g.
`Some("anthropic")` for builtin_claude_sonnet/builtin_claude_opus,
`Some("openai")` for builtin_codex (dispatch/mod.rd:450,477), `None` for
builtin_opencode. It already backs `AgentAdapter::gen_ai_system()`
(dispatch/mod.rd:320-322, defaults to "local") and rate-limit provider
checks, and already flows into telemetry event *data* for
RateLimitWait/RateLimitAllowed/MendRateLimitCleaned
(telemetry/mod.rs:1493-1498,1503-1505,1764-1775, sourced from
adapter.provider.clone() at dispatch/mod.rs:1652).

It is NOT currently added as an OTLP resource or record attribute anywhere
in otlp.rs, so the value that answers "which company is providing
inference for this worker" -- e.g. for the dashboard.ardenone.com/needle/
worker cards -- cannot be shown. This was raised as UI feedback on that
dashboard 2026-08-16 ("Add another attribute: model provider. It's the
company that's providing the inference.").

## Request

Add `needle.model.provider` following the same dual-layer pattern
ADR-016 established for needle.agent/needle.model (decision table,
"Identity that changes belongs on the record, not the Resource"):
provider can change per-dispatch whenever agent.routing selects a
different adapter, same as model/agent, so:

  OtlpSink::build_resource() alongside the existing needle.agent/
  needle.model resource attributes.
- Record layer: the actually-dispatched adapter's provider, added

  attributes into emit_log -- this bead's work should land alongside

  mechanism. Check needle-5d246a6d's status/assignee before starting

issue.description:
## Symptom

A single worker's stderr log grew to 33.7 GB and was still growing at ~159 GB/hr
when killed. On lab (2026-08-05) this consumed 33 GB of a 444 GB disk in under
30 minutes and was ~50 minutes from filling the root filesystem.

Observed on worker `claude-print-opus-alpha`, workspace `cgov-polish-queue`,
needle 0.2.15.

## Evidence

Each log line carries its full tracing span stack, and the stack never unwinds:

    worker.session{...}:bead.claim{...}:bead.lifecycle{...}:bead.claim{...}:bead.lifecycle{...}...

Measured within one session, same event type:

| sample | bead.claim depth | bead.lifecycle depth | longest line |
|--------|------------------|----------------------|--------------|
| early  | 18               | 18                   | 4,983 bytes  |
| late   | 2,488            | 2,488                | 629,829 bytes |

The two depths are exactly equal, and grow by one pair per claim cycle. Because
every subsequent event re-serializes the whole accumulated stack, total output
grows quadratically — which is why the rate was unremarkable at first and
reached 159 GB/hr about 20 minutes in.

## Root cause

`src/worker/mod.rs:1608`

    self.bead_lifecycle_span = Some(lifecycle_span.entered());

`EnteredSpan` is a RAII guard over the thread-local span stack, which requires
LIFO drop order. On the next claim this line evaluates in the wrong order:

1. `lifecycle_span.entered()` pushes the NEW span onto the stack
2. the assignment then drops the OLD `EnteredSpan`, popping it

The old guard is no longer on top when it drops, so the exit is out of order and
the previous span is never removed. One `bead.lifecycle` leaks per claim cycle.

The same defect hits `bead.claim` at `src/worker/mod.rs:1552`:

    let _claim_enter = claim_span.enter();

`_claim_enter` is dropped at end of scope, i.e. AFTER line 1608 has already
pushed the lifecycle span on top of it — again out of order. This is why
`bead.claim` and `bead.lifecycle` accumulate at identical depth.

The comment at `src/worker/mod.rs:1610` asserts the claim span "is dropped here",
which is not what the code does.

## Deliverables

- Fix the guard ordering so each claim cycle exits its spans LIFO. Options:
  explicitly drop the previous `bead_lifecycle_span` before entering the new one;
  drop `_claim_enter` before line 1608; or stop holding `EnteredSpan` across
  await points / in struct fields and use `Span` + `.in_scope()` / `Instrument`.
- Note: holding an `EnteredSpan` across an `.await` (line 1560) is itself unsound
  for async and is worth removing regardless.
- Add a bound / guard so a runaway span stack can never again produce
  multi-hundred-KB log lines.

## Acceptance criteria

- A worker running >=200 consecutive claim cycles shows constant span depth in
  stderr — not monotonically increasing.
- Regression test asserts span depth after N claims is O(1), not O(N).
- Max observed log line length stays bounded across a long run.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt` clean.

## Repro / artifacts

Samples preserved on lab at `.needle/logs/samples/alpha-stderr-{head,tail}-2MB.log`
(relative to the coding user's home). The head sample shows depth 18, the tail
sample depth 2,488, same session `d5813a0d`.
issue.notes:
[migrated notes from bf-3uj6i]
Implemented and pushed commit a34974f: replaced cross-await EnteredSpan guards with async instrumentation, stored bead.lifecycle as Span, added a 64 KiB tracing line cap for file/stderr writers, and added a 200-cycle depth/line regression. Targeted regressions, log-writer tests, mitosis/knot tests, modified-file rustfmt, and cargo clippy --lib --bins -- -D warnings pass. Local cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings reaches a pre-existing clippy::zombie_processes failure in tests/process_discovery_integration.rs:127. Authoritative workflow needle-ci-t7vzh cannot start verification: PVC needle-ci-t7vzh-workspace requests 2Gi with storage class ssd, while the Rackspace provisioner requires 5-20Gi; workflow remains Pending/Unschedulable and prior needle-ci-6d5d5 is stuck on the same condition. Per repository policy, leaving bead open until CI infrastructure is repaired and a workflow succeeds.

[migrated comment from bf-3uj6i, 2026-08-05T20:33:26.472209206Z, author cli]
ROOT CAUSE CORRECTION (verified against tracing-subscriber 0.3.23 source). The stated mechanism -- non-LIFO exit leaving the previous span un-popped -- does not hold. SpanStack::pop does a reverse search and stack.remove(idx), so it removes the span from anywhere in the stack, not just the top; an out-of-order exit on a single thread is harmless. The mechanism that actually leaks is the one noted only in passing at the end of the bead: holding the EnteredSpan across .await. On a multi-thread runtime the task resumes on another thread, the guard drops there, that stack has no matching id, pop() returns false, and the original thread's entry is orphaned. Fixed in c2d83c3 by switching to .instrument(). Note for auditing other enter() call sites: the rule is 'never hold a guard across await', not 'preserve LIFO order'.

cycling, disk, telemetry, umbrella, worker
issue.title: fix(worker): unbounded tracing span nesting on claim path floods stderr at ~159 GB/hr
